newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Second tier Russian shares show gains at open RSA1 LCE.
newsitem.headline: Second tier Russian shares show gains at open RSA1 LCE.

text.p: Lukewarm support by Russian investors lifted prices of some leading shares at the open on Thursday but traders said domestic investors were distracted by the T-bill market and foreign investors were on the sidelines.
Traders saw best growth potential in the short and medium term among lower-tier oil stocks, as well as some telecoms and energy utilities sought by those foreign buyers who were actively trading.

At 0940 GMT, Sakhalinmorneftegaz SKGZ.RTS had risen on a single trade to $2.98 from $2.75 on March 6, when it last traded. Lenenergo preferred shares LSNG_p.RTS had firmed to $0.645 from $0.600 at Wednesday's close.
Chelyabenergo CHNG.RTS rose to $0.48 from $0.46 on 2.7 million shares turnover and Irkutskenergo IRGZ.RTS fell to $0.2650 from $0.2725.
Brunswick trader Gary Kinsey said some Russian brokers were bidding in roubles to make selling difficult by foreigners holding dollar-denominated shares.
American Depositary Receipts were generally trading at a discount to the market, indicating some foreign reluctance to buy, Kinsey said, adding he had not seen major sellers.

Kirill Maltsev, institutional sales manager at Rye Man and Gor Securities said Russians were supporting leading shares but that domestic interest had waned recently on rising yields in the domestic treasury bill market.
Yields on GKO discount T-bills have risen solidly into the 30s and hit 40 in some issues while the market was near 30 a couple of weeks ago.
The launch of Russia's two billion mark Eurobond, with a nine percent coupon and seven year maturity, failed to affect shares. It was priced to yield 370 basis points over Bunds.
Traders were mixed whether new cabinet appointments, expected any day now, would cause a sharp reaction since reformers are expected.
